summary.title: Writing is Thinking: Learning to Write with Confidence
summary.one_liner: Writing and thinking reinforce each other, and you can make writing easier by separating ideation, outlining, research and drafting into passive and active steps that lower the activation energy to start.
takeaways: Writing and thinking are two linked processes: improving one improves the other, and a clear point of view reduces the mental load of writing.
Split the work into separate passive (ideation, idea arbitrage) and active (tracking, outlining, research, writing) stages to avoid one overwhelming pass.
Start from a low-friction capture habit: note ideas in a doc, check whether they already exist online, and let outlines marinate before drafting.
Optimize for one variable such as quality rather than speed, SEO and output at the same time.
Tools the author mentions include Draftback for reviewing revision history, Readwise for Kindle highlights, Weava highlighter, and Ahrefs, Keyword Planner and Keywords Everywhere for SEO research.
summary.summary: The author, a blogger who leads a publications team, describes a personal writing process built on the idea that writing is thinking. The core method is to separate the work into six steps (ideation, tracking, outline, idea arbitrage, research, writing), alternating passive and active states to lower the activation energy needed to begin. The post also covers choosing quality as a single guiding priority, using Draftback to review revision history, and tools for highlights and keyword research. It is a first-person essay with quotes from other books, not a step-by-step technical tutorial.
